audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Linguistics degree studies how languages are structured, how they change, and how people acquire and use them. In Descriptive Linguistics, students compare languages and learn to analyse and document them through fieldwork.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table retains 175 distinct EC in Descriptive Linguistics. Berber is counted once despite appearing in two years of the catalogue. The archived Leti rotation is a plausible route to the remaining 5 EC, but the applicable distinct course or approved replacement for this intake still needs confirmation.

curriculum.limitation: The degree requires 180 EC; this partial record lists 175 distinct EC. The remaining 5 EC rotation is unconfirmed for this intake. First-year course sets are available in Dutch or English; the post-first-year Descriptive Linguistics specialisation is taught in English.

componentNotes.ling-y1-sociolinguistics: Studies language variation, multilingualism, social identity, register and the ways individuals, groups and authorities use language to organise social life.
componentNotes.ling-y1-phonology: Introduces phonemes, features, syllables, stress and tone, with practice in analysing the sound structure of languages.
componentNotes.ling-y1-indo-europeans: Introduces language families and comparative reconstruction through Proto-Indo-European, its daughter languages and the culture and prehistory of their speakers.
componentNotes.ling-y1-digital-humanities: Studies media, data and AI in humanities research through practical assignments and a portfolio, with attention to how digital tools shape knowledge.
componentNotes.ling-y1-syntax: Studies word classes, grammatical categories, constituents and hierarchical sentence structure, including an introduction to generative syntax.
componentNotes.ling-y1-world-languages: Introduces the distribution, diversity, classification and vitality of world languages, using linguistic puzzles and examples of grammatical structures.
componentNotes.ling-y1-speech-sounds: Develops the production, recognition, transcription and analysis of consonants, vowels and tone through lectures and practical work.
componentNotes.ling-y1-communication: Studies intended meaning, indirect communication, speech acts, inference and politeness, alongside turn-taking and coherence in spoken and written discourse.
componentNotes.ling-y1-historical: Studies change in sounds, words, grammar and meaning, language contact and the comparative method. Basic phonology, phonetics and IPA knowledge is expected.
componentNotes.ling-y1-morphology: Studies word formation and inflection, including their interaction with syntax, pronunciation and meaning.
componentNotes.ling-y1-quechua: Required first-year preparation for Descriptive Linguistics. Uses Ayacucho Quechua to study phonology, morphology and syntax through translation, glossing and formulation exercises; it is not a fluency course.
componentNotes.ling-y1-word-meaning: Required first-year preparation for Descriptive Linguistics. Studies lexical meanings and relations, metaphor, connotations across languages and the principles of dictionary description.
componentNotes.ling-y2-descriptive: Develops analysis of relatively unprocessed phonological, morphological and syntactic data from little-analysed languages, individually and in groups.
componentNotes.ling-y2-typology: Compares grammatical patterns within and across languages and explores their distribution, history and relationship to description and fieldwork. Introductory linguistics or an equivalent background is required.
componentNotes.ling-y2-sign-gesture: Studies the structures, use and transmission of sign languages and gestures, with video recording and annotation in ELAN. It is a linguistic study course rather than sign-language acquisition.
componentNotes.ling-y2-language-use: Studies cross-cultural norms of verbal and non-verbal communication, including status, politics, knowledge and oral traditions, building on language-and-communication concepts.
componentNotes.ling-y2-fieldwork: Works with a speaker of an unfamiliar or underdescribed language to collect and analyse data for a basic grammar sketch, including elicitation, recordings, documentation ethics and a student database. Prior Speech Sounds study is advised.
componentNotes.ling-y2-berber: Counted once. Studies Tarifiyt Berber grammar through transcribed texts and its cultural context, rather than spoken-language acquisition. The course is offered biennially. Its repeated catalogue listing does not establish another distinct 5 EC.
componentNotes.ling-y2-prehistory: Uses historical classification, language contact and traces of lost languages to investigate prehistory, including comparison with archaeology and genetics. A foundation in historical-linguistic methods is expected.
componentNotes.ling-5512vev10y: Illustrated 10 EC restricted choice from another Linguistics specialisation. Introduces Vedic Sanskrit phonology and morphology and its relation to Proto-Indo-European; basic linguistics and Indo-European reconstruction knowledge is required.
componentNotes.ling-5512vcg01y: Illustrated 5 EC restricted choice. Develops propositional and predicate logic, basic proofs and their relationship to natural language, including applications in semantics, acquisition and computational research.
componentNotes.ling-5000vphscy: Studies scientific and humanities methods, including Popper, Kuhn and Foucault, and reflection on scholarly inquiry. The current course is taught in English.
componentNotes.ling-5733k2014y: Studies language as culturally embedded and socially situated practice, including linguistic relativity, naming, narrative and cultural knowledge, with ethnographic observation and comparative cases.
componentNotes.ling-5170v10y: Illustrated third-year 5 EC restricted choice. Introduces corpus collection and preparation, word frequencies, concordances, collocations and keywords, combining digital results with critical interpretation. No prior programming is required.
componentNotes.ling-y3-thesis: A supervised investigation within the specialisation, with a research question, method, results and conclusion. Participation in the accompanying seminar is mandatory within these 10 EC; the seminar adds no credits. The proposal goes to the Board of Examiners after supervisor confirmation.
componentNotes.ling-krb30s1: Open study may include a minor, approved individual package, internship or study abroad. Individual packages need sufficient level and no overlap with compulsory study; normally no more than 10 EC is introductory and at least 10 EC is advanced. Recognised full 30 EC Leiden, Delft or Erasmus minors have an approval exemption; Honours courses cannot count. Internships need approval before starting. For this specialisation, overlapping courses in the Second-Language Acquisition minor must be replaced with approved alternatives.
